tsa-ice-dhs-shutdown.context:
CONTEXT: The post-9/11 airport security state and its fractures

ORIGINS
2001  Nineteen hijackers seized four airliners on September 11, crashing them into the World Trade Center, the Pentagon, and a Pennsylvania field — the attacks that restructured American domestic security.
2001  Congress passed the Aviation and Transportation Security Act, creating the Transportation Security Administration to consolidate air travel security under a single federal agency.
2002  The Homeland Security Act established the Department of Homeland Security and reorganized the federal government, passing the Senate 90–9.
2002  TSA was transferred from the Department of Transportation into the new DHS.
2002  Immigration and Customs Enforcement was created under the same act, absorbing the functions of the Immigration and Naturalization Service and the United States Customs Service.

THE APPARATUS
TSA holds authority over the security of all transportation systems within and connecting to the United States.
ICE's stated mission covers criminal investigations, immigration enforcement, national security, and public safety — a mandate broad enough to operate well beyond borders.
The FAA, a separate agency under the Department of Transportation, regulates civil aviation including air traffic control, personnel certification, and airport standards.
DHS itself is responsible for anti-terrorism, border control, immigration, cybersecurity, transportation security, and maritime security — the largest post-9/11 reorganization of federal power.

SHUTDOWN MECHANICS
A government shutdown occurs when Congress fails to enact funding legislation before the fiscal year begins.
During a shutdown, federal agencies curtail services, cease non-essential operations, and furlough non-essential workers.
Only employees deemed essential — those protecting human life or property — are retained on duty without pay.
TSA screeners, classified as essential, must continue working through shutdowns unpaid.

THE AIRPORT
LaGuardia Airport sits on 680 acres in East Elmhurst, Queens, on the northwestern shore of Long Island bordering Flushing Bay.
The facility was established in 1929 and began operating as a public airport in 1939, named after former New York City mayor Fiorello La Guardia.

WHY IT MATTERS
Aviation safety is the study and practice of managing risks across all aspects of flight, from personnel training to infrastructure design.
Adverse weather, turbulence, icing, and reduced visibility are recognized as major contributing factors to safety outcomes — but so is institutional failure to act on known risks.
The post-9/11 security apparatus was built to prevent catastrophic failure, yet its workforce — the people who physically operate it — can be forced to work without pay whenever Congress stalls on funding.
tsa-ice-dhs-shutdown.label: TSA workers unpaid in second shutdown as ICE militarizes airports

iran-us-israel-war.context:
CONTEXT: Iran, the United States, and Israel — From Alliance to War

ORIGINS
1856  Persia's first encounters with America; the US seen as trustworthy compared to Britain and Russia during the Great Game.
1953  CIA and MI6 overthrew Prime Minister Mohammad Mosaddegh, ending Iran's democratic experiment and installing Shah Pahlavi as a Western client.
1979  Iranian Revolution toppled the Shah; the Islamic Republic severed all ties with both the United States and Israel.
1979  Iran adopted the elimination of Israel as a Jewish state as a core foreign policy; Israel began treating Iran as an existential threat.

THE STRAIT
The Strait of Hormuz is 104 miles long and as narrow as 24 miles wide, connecting the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman.
Iran holds the northern shore; the UAE and Oman's Musandam exclave hold the south.
Every tanker leaving the Gulf must pass through it — whoever controls the strait controls the flow.

THE FIRST HORMUZ WAR
1980  Iraq invaded Iran; eight years of war killed 500,000.
1981-1988  The Tanker War: Iran and Iraq attacked merchant shipping in the Gulf and the Strait; Iraq struck 283 vessels, Iran struck 168.
1981  Israel destroyed Iraq's unfinished nuclear reactor in Operation Opera, establishing the Begin Doctrine — a standing policy to strike any regional nuclear capability.

NUCLEAR STANDOFF
2015  Iran nuclear deal framework reached between Iran and the P5+1 powers plus the EU.
The deal's collapse reopened the question of Iran's nuclear ambitions and gave Israel justification under the Begin Doctrine to escalate.

ESCALATION
Iran funded, trained, and armed militant groups hostile to Israel across the region, including Ansar Allah (Houthis) in Yemen, a Zaydi Shia military organization and part of Iran's Axis of Resistance.
Israel targeted Iranian assets through assassinations, airstrikes, and covert operations against its nuclear program.
2025-2026  The hostility escalated into large-scale armed conflict between Iran and Israel.

THE GULF STATES
1981  The Gulf Cooperation Council established — Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, UAE — a military alliance sitting on the southern shore of the conflict zone.
These states now weigh military entry as the Hormuz blockade tightens and the war reaches their waters.

NOW
Pakistani and Afghan clerics call to extend a pause to Eid al-Adha, the festival of sacrifice falling on the 10th of Dhu al-Hijja.
Diplomatic signals are increasingly contradictory — ceasefire appeals alongside military posturing.

ISLAMIC CONTEXT
"And if they incline to peace, then incline to it [also] and rely upon Allah. Indeed, it is He who is the Hearing, the Knowing." — Quran 8:61
Ibn Kathir: This verse commands acceptance of genuine peace overtures, citing the Prophet's acceptance of the Treaty of Hudaybiyah and his instruction, "There will be disputes after me, so if you have a way to end them in peace, then do so."
iran-us-israel-war.label: Iran-US-Israel war: Gulf states weigh military entry, Hormuz blockade tightens
